title: The retail age floor and the thirty-day extension power
rule_summary: In the retail drug business setting collaborative practice is limited to PATIENTS 18 YEARS OF AGE OR OLDER; to AN EXTENSION BY 30 DAYS of current drug therapy prescribed by the supervising physician; and to administration of vaccines or the modification of dosages of medications prescribed by the supervising physician for the named disease states and co-morbidities identified by the supervising physician for the individual patient along with the primary diagnosis.
exam_relevance: Tests the retail age floor and the shape of the extension power, which extends existing therapy rather than initiating new therapy.

numeric_facts.fact: Retail collaborative practice minimum patient age
Maximum extension of current drug therapy in the retail setting
numeric_facts.conditions: therapy prescribed by the supervising physician

common_confusions: Treating the extension power as a power to initiate therapy
Extending a therapy the supervising physician did not prescribe
Assuming the age floor is a guideline rather than a statutory limit
